title: Pronunciation & intonation
examples: How do I make my voice sound more interested when I read?
What is the difference between stress and intonation?
Can you give me an example of falling intonation?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how we say words.

items: Intonation: the rise and fall of your voice

explain.say: Word stress means putting extra force on one part of a word.
For example, in the word 'pho-TO-graph', we stress the middle syllable.
Rising intonation means your voice goes up at the end of a sentence.
A falling intonation means your voice goes down at the end of a sentence.
When we talk about lists, we usually use a rising tone for each item.

faq.q: How do I know which syllable to stress in a new word?
faq.a: Sometimes you just have to listen to a native speaker say it. You can also look up the word in a dictionary.
asks: Where can I find the stress pattern?
Does the dictionary show stress marks?

faq.q: When is it okay to use a rising intonation?
faq.a: You use it when you are asking a question that expects a 'yes' or 'no' answer. It shows you are seeking confirmation.
asks: What tone do I use for questions?
Does my voice sound higher for questions?

faq.q: What is the difference between stress and intonation?
faq.a: Stress is about the force on one syllable within a word. Intonation is about the overall pitch change across a whole sentence.
asks: Are they related or different things?

faq.q: If I speak too quickly, does it affect my intonation?
faq.a: Yes, speaking too fast can make your pitch changes sound unclear. Try pausing slightly between main ideas.
asks: Should I speak slowly when I talk?
How does speed affect my voice?

faq.q: Do I always use a falling tone at the end of a statement?
faq.a: Generally, yes, a falling tone signals that you have finished making a statement. It sounds final and certain.
asks: When should my voice go down?
Is a flat tone okay at the end?

facts: Stress is the emphasis placed on a particular syllable within a word.
Rising intonation often signals that a question is being asked.
Falling intonation typically marks the end of a statement or thought.
A sentence's overall pitch change is called intonation.

quiz.say: Which syllable should be stressed in the word 'ele-PHANT'?

options.show: The first and second syllables equally
options.say: The first and second syllables equally

quiz.why: The stress falls on the second syllable, 'PHANT', which makes the word sound correct.

wrong.1: This is a common mistake because the first part of the word is often the longest sound.
wrong.2: This is wrong because stress requires placing more force on only one part.
wrong.3: This is tempting because many words end with the strongest sound.

quiz.say: What does a rising intonation usually signal at the end of a phrase?
quiz.why: Your voice going up shows the listener you are expecting an answer.

wrong.0: A pause is silence; rising tone is a change in pitch.
wrong.1: While lists use rising tones, the primary signal is questioning.
wrong.3: Strong statements usually end with a falling tone to sound final.

quiz.say: If you are listing three items, what is the typical pattern of intonation?
quiz.why: You raise your voice for the first two items, and then lower it for the final item.

wrong.0: Using only falling tones makes the list sound like a series of separate statements.
wrong.1: If you rise on the last item, it sounds like you forgot to say something.
wrong.2: This pattern does not fit the natural rhythm of completing a list.
